newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur barges up on buying, cargo steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur barges up on buying, cargo steady.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges jumped on Wednesday as concerted buying by one player lifted numbers.
But cargo prices for both low and high sulphur were steady in a listless market, with traders clearing their desks before the long Easter weekend.
High sulphur barges were traded up from Tuesday's $85 fob ARA level to $89 by lunchtime. Offers of $89.50 were not being taken up in the afternoon by the dominant buyer.
Traders speculated that the buying was tied to a medium-sized cargo sale.
"The market is so thin it's very easy to move prices at the moment," said one fuel oil seller.
Bunker interest was healthy, with buyers satisfying physical requirements ahead of the four-day weekend.
Traders said there was little real support for either the low or high sulphur market.
Activity was very limited on the low sulphur spot market, although a U.K. refiner sold a small packet of above average quality cracked material at an undisclosed price.
Low sulphur availabilities were said to be tight in the prompt period but good from mid to late April.
